page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-192-lssd is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor. It features 192 dedicated vCPUs across 96 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base speed of 2.3 GHz. The processor includes a 504 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. System memory capacity is 720.0 GB, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per core. The server is equipped with 12599 GB of local NVMe SSD storage across 32 local SSDs, with no bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in multi-core CPU execution, including stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU score, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the middle 50 percent, though Geekbench single-core reaches the top 10 percent. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with both small-block cached and large-block uncached read operations scoring in the top 10 percent. Database operations and Redis SET operations also rank in the top 10 percent, alongside static web serving throughput. Large-model LLM inference achieves strong prompt processing but falls to average speeds for text generation.

This server offers high resource density, combining massive compute capacity with a substantial local NVMe SSD storage array. The qualitative cost efficiency is driven by the integration of 32 local SSDs, which eliminates the need for external storage attachments for high-throughput database workloads. However, the 3.75 GB RAM-per-core ratio represents a potential tradeoff for memory-bound workloads that require larger memory footprints per execution thread. The presence of advanced instruction sets, such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions, enhances compute efficiency for specialized vector and matrix operations without requiring discrete GPU hardware.

Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-192-lssd is suited for high-throughput database operations, large-scale software compilation, multi-threaded data processing, and static web serving. The combination of dedicated Intel Xeon cores and extensive local NVMe storage supports intensive I/O workloads, while the AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets facilitate CPU-based machine learning inference and cryptographic tasks.
